A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FastDINOv2 work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, corruption robustness, instance recognition, segmentation, computational-cost, and ablation results in Sections 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds SimCLR experiments, transition-schedule ablations, and convergence-time measurements in Appendices A.4–A.6.

M1.justification: The downsampling procedure, 75/25 curriculum, optimizer restart, and second-stage Gaussian noise patching remain unchanged. Appendix A.4 applies the existing curriculum to SimCLR with a ResNet backbone; it does not introduce a new curriculum component or modify its operations.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-100, ImageNet-1K and their corruption counterparts, Oxford/Paris instance recognition, and ADE20K segmentation. The new experiments reuse ImageNet-100 and ImageNet-100-C; framework and schedule variations do not add dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 10 evaluates a SimCLR baseline against FastSimCLR, adding one comparison framework beyond the existing DINOv2 experiments. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendices A.4–A.6 add a ResNet/SimCLR experiment using LARS and matched 200-epoch budgets, five curriculum stage proportions at a fixed 200-epoch budget, and timing measurements to reach 55%, 65%, 75%, and 78% accuracy. These are focused additions to evaluation settings; the earlier experimental protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 newly tests transition timing, including full-resolution-only and low-resolution-only controls. Appendix A.6 adds analysis of when convergence gains emerge. These extend the existing resolution, augmentation, batch-size, positional-embedding, and frequency analyses with targeted checks of schedule choice and convergence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. New Tables 10–12 continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty. A.5 calls its schedule sweep 'cross validation' but specifies no folds, repetitions, or statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their values. New Table 10 reports SimCLR/FastSimCLR clean accuracies of 64.48%/64.82%, corruption accuracies of 30.95%/38.73%, and training times of 14/11.2 A6000 hours. Table 11 finds 75/25 best among tested schedules at 78.1%; Table 12 reports 23.04/13.1 hours for DINOv2/FastDINOv2 to reach 78%. These are additional results, not revisions to earlier scores.

T1.justification: The cropping definition and bicubic kernel, interpolation, and coordinate equations remain mathematically unchanged (Equations 1–4). No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about faster DINOv2 training, reduced computation, competitive clean accuracy, and corruption robustness. The appendix additions support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: A.5 explains how insufficient low-resolution training limits efficiency while excessive low-resolution training limits exposure to full-resolution features. A.6 attributes similar early convergence and later acceleration to frequency bias and useful initialization. A.4 adds evidence of applicability to SimCLR/CNNs; the existing fixed-schedule limitation remains.

D1.justification: The new experiments document LARS, a ResNet backbone, training-stage budgets, and A6000 timing hardware. Tables 2 and 8 newly specify a single-GPU basis for L40S timing measurements, without establishing that earlier experiments were rerun. Code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the 39 cited works are retained, including the existing SimCLR reference. The new SimCLR comparison does not revise the novelty argument or positioning relative to previous curriculum-learning and robustness research.

P1.justification: Three appendix subsections are inserted, the former A.4 becomes A.7, and its cross-reference is updated. Other edits are limited to wording, GPU naming, and replacing the preprint notice with a NeurIPS 2025 conference notice; the main narrative is otherwise stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–12, relocates the retained appendix visualizations, and adjusts timing captions and table spacing. Figure 1 uses a higher-resolution rendering of the same diagram. The existing analysis figures retain their image content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the justification for the previously heuristic 75/25 schedule, tests transfer to SimCLR/ResNet, and measures efficiency at matched accuracy targets. These additions provide useful supporting evidence without removing earlier results. Their scope remains limited, and uncertainty estimates and some new-experiment details, such as the ResNet variant, remain unspecified, so the overall improvement is modest.
